articles.title: What fish are fusiform shaped?
articles.summary: Fish like tuna, mackerel, and salmon possess a fusiform, streamlined body shape, a key evolutionary adaptation for achieving high speed and efficiency in water. This design significantly minimizes drag, enabling these predatory species to conserve energy while effectively pursuing prey. Understanding such natural biological designs can offer valuable insights into biomimicry and engineering principles for efficient transport systems, showcasing nature's elegant solutions in marine life.

articles.title: On the verge of strikes in Iran, the US held off. What happens next is up to Trump
articles.summary: President Donald Trump's national security officials convened a late-night Situation Room meeting to deliberate potential military options against Iran. Emerging from the Tuesday discussions, officials felt a decision on striking Iran was likely imminent. This development highlighted significant geopolitical tensions and the possibility of direct military engagement, prompting close scrutiny of international relations and strategic implications.

articles.title: Cash, luxury items seized
articles.summary: Malaysian authorities confiscated over RM50mil in assets, cash, and frozen account funds during two high-profile investigations involving the military. This significant seizure highlights ongoing efforts to combat corruption and ensure integrity within the armed forces. Such probes underscore the importance of accountability and ethical conduct among personnel, a crucial aspect for aspiring defence officers.

articles.title: MACC to meet Mindef leaders next Wednesday
articles.summary: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief, Tan Sri Azam Baki, announced upcoming discussions with Malaysia's Defence Ministry next week in Putrajaya. The meeting's purpose will likely address transparency and governance within the defence sector, highlighting ongoing efforts to combat corruption in state institutions. This initiative underscores Malaysia's commitment to good governance and accountability in public administration.

articles.title: MACC to wrap up two Army graft cases soon
articles.summary: Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief, Tan Sri Azam Baki, announced from Putrajaya that two significant corruption cases involving several top military officers are anticipated to conclude by next week. This signals a proactive national effort to address accountability within Malaysia's defence sector, underscoring commitment to transparency and integrity in the armed forces. Such actions are vital for maintaining public trust and military discipline.
